notes:
BLIND arm. Answered only from documented biography (Wikipedia on Lennon / Julia Lennon / Cynthia Lennon / Alfred Lennon / Murder of John Lennon; Beatles Bible day-by-day entries; Lewisohn and Norman via secondary reporting; the 2024 Ophthalmic & Physiological Optics paper on his myopia; Lennon v. INS 527 F.2d 187; Green's Dakota Days; contemporaneous press). Part D omitted - this exercise forbade opening any reading, and no astrology source of any kind was consulted or read.

Born 9 Oct 1940, Liverpool Maternity Hospital, Oxford Street (hence B5=hospital). A1/A2/A3: the widely repeated 6.30 pm figure traces to Aunt Mimi Smith's recollection, not to a record - English birth certificates of the period did not record time of birth except for multiple births - so 'family_memory' and 'round_hour' (a half-hour figure); no rectification is documented either way, hence A3=unknown. Mimi's associated air-raid story is disproven: Liverpool was not bombed that night.

A4/A5: exactly one true hospital admission is documented - five days at Lawson Memorial Hospital, Golspie, 1-6 July 1969 after crashing his Austin Maxi near Loch Eriboll (17 stitches to the chin). He was taken to Roosevelt Hospital on 8 Dec 1980 with no pulse and a resuscitative thoracotomy was performed; he was pronounced dead at 11.15 pm. I did not count that terminal, unsuccessful procedure as either a lifetime admission or a surgery, so A5='none' - no elective or therapeutic surgery is on record anywhere in his life. If the scorer counts the thoracotomy, A4 becomes 'two_three' and A5 'one'.

A6: eyes is the single best-documented body area - myopia found at about age seven, moderate astigmatism, failed contact-lens years 1963-67, and the 2024 optometry paper judges the degree such that it would likely have worsened into a threat to vision; his mother and sister were also very nearsighted. 'nerves' covers the heavily documented depression, heroin addiction and methadone withdrawal ('Cold Turkey'), insomnia and the six months of primal therapy with Arthur Janov (1 Apr - 15 Sep 1970). No recurring digestive, cardiac or respiratory complaint is documented despite heavy smoking, so those were left out rather than guessed.

A7/A8: no childhood illness of note is recorded and no personal peril before age eight is documented; he was an infant in Liverpool through the Blitz, which is context rather than a documented personal danger, so 'no' rather than 'yes'. A9: Jack Lennon 1855-1921 (66), Mary 'Polly' Maguire 1874-1949 (75), George Ernest Stanley 1874-1949 (75), Annie Jane Millward 1873-1941 (68) - mean about 71.

A10 'absent': Alfred went absent without leave in Feb 1944 and there was no contact for close to twenty years; the 1964 reunion at NEMS lasted twenty minutes ('What do you want?') and Lennon broke off relations again after Alfred's 1965 cash-in single, though he phoned his father on his deathbed in 1976. 'conflicted' is the alternative; absence is the longer-running fact. A11 'reversal': the seaman's pay cheques stopped when he deserted. A12 'died_early': Julia was killed by a car driven by off-duty policeman Eric Clague on 15 July 1958 when John was 17 - though she had also given his care to Mimi around 1946, so 'absent' is a defensible second reading; the Blackpool 'choose between your parents' scene is disputed by Lewisohn. A13 'distant': half-sisters Julia Baird (b. 1947) and Jacqui Dykins (b. 1949) - regular contact in the early 1950s, last in-person meeting 1967, then no contact until a surprise call in 1975; half-sister Victoria/Ingrid was adopted out in 1945 and he never knew of her; paternal half-brothers David (1969) and Robin (1973) he effectively never knew.

A14/A15: Dovedale Primary, Quarry Bank High School 1952-57 (dropped from the A to the C stream, failed all his O-levels), then Liverpool College of Art 1957-60, thrown out before his final year - so the highest COMPLETED level is school, and the interruption was serious. A16/A17/A18: self-employed musician/songwriter through Beatles Ltd, Northern Songs and Apple Corps, plus two published books (In His Own Write 1964, A Spaniard in the Works 1965) and film work - 'own_business' with design_art and writing_media; no salaried employment is documented. A19 'about_right' is a judgement call on an artist with 25 US number ones as performer or writer.

A21 'net_gain' is investment rather than betting - no gambling is documented; the Ono-run portfolio (600-acre Franklin NY dairy farm bought 1978, Holstein herd, Dakota apartments, Egyptian artefacts) is documented as very profitable, including a cow sold for about $250,000-$265,000 in 1980, and he died worth roughly $200m. A22 'none': no inheritance or windfall is documented at any point. A23 'serious_past' rests on the 1968-69 Apple crisis and his own Disc and Music Echo statement that all four would be 'broke in six months' - contested, since McCartney later called it a figure of speech, and Lennon was never personally insolvent; 'manageable' is the alternative and C10 is therefore rated confidence 2.

A24 'married': he was married to Yoko Ono at his death. A25 gives the first marriage (Cynthia Powell, 23 Aug 1962, at 21 and precipitated by pregnancy - early against his own parents, who married at 26 and 24); Cynthia's decree nisi came 8 Nov 1968; he married Ono in Gibraltar 20 Mar 1969, separated Oct 1973 to Jan 1975 (the 'lost weekend' with May Pang), then reunited - hence A27 'mixed'. A28 two acknowledged children, Julian (8 Apr 1963) and Sean (9 Oct 1975). A29 'yes': Ono miscarried John Ono Lennon II on 21 Nov 1968 at Queen Charlotte's and lost a second son in Oct 1969; further losses are reported but not publicly documented.

A30: 'outspoken' and 'quick_tempered' are as well evidenced as anything in his life (the 'rattle your jewellery' quip, the 1966 'more popular than Jesus' remark, school fights, the 1974 Troubadour incidents, his own Playboy admission of having been physically cruel to women, 'Jealous Guy'); 'bold' from the peace campaigns and the MBE return; 'solitary' from his own account of himself and the 1975-80 Dakota withdrawal; 'philosophical' from Imagine, 'God' and the primal-therapy period. A31 'extended' - the 1965 'Help!'/'Fat Elvis' depression, heroin, the post-1972-election collapse, primal therapy. A32 'strong' rather than 'central': Transcendental Meditation with the Maharishi in 1967-68 and Rishikesh in 1968, a 1977 born-again phase, and the documented 1975-80 governance of travel and decisions by Ono's numerologists and tarot reader John Green ('Charlie Swan'). (Recording this as biographical fact only - no astrological material about him was read.) A33 'abroad' - Hamburg from 1960, then New York from 13 Aug 1971 until his death. A34 'brief' - the five hospital days in 1969; he was never imprisoned or institutionalised.

A35: twelve of about sixteen datable turning points fit the cap. Omitted for space: the move to Mimi's at Mendips (c.1945-46), the 1965 MBE and its 1970 return, the Oct 1973 separation from Ono, Alfred's death 1 Apr 1976, the green card won 27 July 1976 after the four-year INS deportation fight begun Mar 1972, the Aug-Nov 1980 Double Fantasy comeback, and his murder on 8 Dec 1980. A36 'same' is a null answer - he has been dead since 1980, so no post-2023 comparison exists and the question has no valid option.

B1 opt1 is unambiguous for him. B2 'lean_tall' - about 5 ft 11 in and habitually slim apart from the 1965 weight gain he himself resented. B3 'right' is genuinely undocumented; no source discusses how people guessed his age, so the neutral option was taken. B4 'eldest' - first-born of Julia's five children, though raised effectively as an only child. B6 omits own_surgery because none is documented, and takes first_job as the 48-night Hamburg residency from Aug 1960, his first sustained paid professional work (a brief labouring job that summer is reported but poorly sourced).

Part C reasoning. C1 both: Ono's management multiplied his fortune, but the Apple/Klein wars and the Cynthia settlement sit on the other side. C2 difficulty: his spiritual search is a documented sequence of disillusionments - the Maharishi and 'Sexy Sadie', 'God' ('I don't believe in...'), an abandoned born-again phase. C3 difficulty, confidence only 3: New York gave him his best solo years but also four years of deportation proceedings, FBI surveillance and the place of his murder. C4 both, high confidence: his tongue made his reputation and repeatedly wrecked it. C5 clearly one way (solidly difficult) - lifelong severe myopia. C6 clearly one way (solidly good) - Kenwood, Tittenhurst, multiple Dakota apartments, the farm, art and artefacts. C7 both - enormous income against the Apple hemorrhage, punitive UK tax and litigation. C8 genuinely both is the single most secure answer on the sheet. C9 'gone well' - no chronic illness; he died at 40 by gunshot, not disease, and addiction was treated as A31/A6 rather than long-term illness. C10 and C11 are the weakest items: no inheritance of any kind is documented as coming to him, and his personal debt position is contested, so both are confidence 2. C12 'gone well' - the 1963-64 Beatlemania windfall.
